ProstoCAD for FreeCAD (formerly InCad) - what changed
================================

This build: VERSION
Newest build first. The build name is the name of the zip file.


0.17.5
----
Improvements
- Extrude, Revolve and the other features take one closed area of a sketch also when its lines do not cross: a sketch with several closed areas (two separate circles, a ring and the disc inside it, a row of shapes) shows its areas, and the one clicked is used (Shift-click takes several, Cmd+A / Ctrl+A all of them, Esc cancels). A sketch with one area is used at once, as before.
- Shell is InCad's own, on OpenCASCADE directly: when the usual way fails, other ways are tried (intersection joins, and walls made from the part and its offset copy), so several walls open at once now work where they failed - a block with rounded or chamfered vertical edges with its top and a side open, two opposite sides open. New: No opening - a closed hollow, no face removed. A part whose shape is faulty (often an imported STEP) is said plainly instead of being offset: that could crash the program. Shells in older files stay as they are.
- Sketch ▸ Tangent Circle works like the other sketch tools: pick it, then click the three lines, arcs or circles the circle touches (construction and projected lines and the axes too) - the third click makes the circle. Two or three selected before still make it at once.
- Sketch tools work tool first: pick the tool, then click in the sketch. Mirror no longer needs the shapes selected before: click a shape (Cmd/Ctrl-click for more), then the mirror line.
- Sketch tools treat normal, construction and projected lines alike: Symmetric, Mirror, Overall Dimension and Offset take all of them (an outline runs through normal and construction lines together, each copy keeps its kind; a point is never part of an Offset). The points marked on a shown sketch include construction and projected geometry, so a feature can pick a rectangle's centre.
- Overall and Center Point Slot snap to the sketch: a click near a point or line (normal, construction or projected) lands on it and the slot is tied there.
- Extrude is ProstoCAD's own now, built on OpenCASCADE directly instead of FreeCAD's Pad and Pocket. A circle sketched on a face and touching the face's edges (a disc inscribed in a block's face), extruded out as a Join, lost half its volume and came out faulty; cut part-way in, it was faulty too, and a Shell after it as well. Now a Join or Cut on a face is built by cutting that face by the profile and closing the part around the new walls: one solid, its volume exact, a test cut and a Shell work on it. A disc resting on a block's top keeps an exact, sound result (it touches only along a line, so it stays a separate piece, and you are told); a Cut that leaves a wall of no thickness (a circle tangent to a side) says so too. A Cut still goes into the part unless flipped. Files with FreeCAD's Pad and Pocket open and edit as before (a file with the new Extrude needs the add-on installed to rebuild it). On a part that is faulty already (such a solid in an imported STEP) Extrude works too; a feature that still fails there says the part is faulty and names it, instead of "invalid geometry".
- Rectangular / Circular Pattern and Mirror are InCad's own, on OpenCASCADE directly: copies touching each other or the part along a line (discs spaced their diameter apart) make one sound solid, the volume exact, every edge sharp, as fast as before. New: Pattern ▸ Solid repeats a whole Solid - joined into it, as one new Solid, or a new Solid per copy - and the copies follow it when it changes. Patterns in older files open as they are and become the new kind, with the same values and parameters, when edited (a file with the new Pattern needs the add-on installed to rebuild it).
- Revolve and Revolve Cut are InCad's own, on OpenCASCADE directly: a full or partial turn, a profile touching the axis or lying along it, and a revolve standing on a face of the part (a disc touching the face's edges) or cut into it each make one sound solid, its volume exact, every edge sharp. The axis line keeps its kind (a normal line stays normal) and is no part of the profile. A revolve across a modeled thread still goes before the thread, at once. Revolves in older files open as they are and become the new kind, with the same values and parameters, when edited; a Pattern repeats the new kind too.

Bug fixes
- Project Geometry in a sketch standing on a face of the part did nothing when an edge or face of that same part was clicked (only other parts and planes could be projected); it now projects it, linked, as from any other place. The plane a sketch stands on still lets the click through.
- Hole ▸ Insert went Through All when the hole had been that before, so the insert's hole ran through the part; choosing Insert now makes it as deep as the insert (M2.5: 6.7 mm).
- Mirror (or a pattern) of a Rectangular / Circular Pattern repeated only the pattern's first feature; it now repeats every copy.
- A minus Spacing in Rectangular Pattern was taken silently and refused only at OK; it now runs the copies the other way.
- A dimension's value box opened at the bottom of the view could go under the Windows taskbar, out of reach; it now stays on the free part of the screen.
- Tangent Circle between two parallel lines: the circle is half the gap across, centred on the mid-line where the pointer is, and the lines stay as drawn (they were tilted to meet a slightly bigger circle); with a third line across them the circle touches it exactly too.
- Extrude: a Join against a taller wall of the part (a block beside a step, joined higher than the step), a Cut Symmetric of a disc inscribed in a face, and a Join or Cut on a part that is faulty already (arcs written as splines in an imported STEP) came out with the right volume but faulty to the full check, and a Shell after them too; a Join Symmetric of such a disc was refused. Now each is one sound solid, its volume exact, and a Shell after it works.
- Revolve about a normal line of the sketch drawn beside the profile (not part of its outline) was refused as a loose piece; the line is now left out of the profile (it keeps its kind) and the revolve is made, as about a construction line there.
- Overall Dimension over two projected circles (two holes of the part) jumped to their inner sides when the part changed (the holes moved apart or got smaller) and measured the gap; it now stays on the outer sides it was placed on.
- Boolean Cut with a round tool as wide as the part (a 20 mm round through a 20 mm wide block, tangent to both walls) was refused as "the solids only touch"; it now cuts, the volume exact, the pieces sound.
- Sketch ▸ Break Link (right-click a projected edge): the edge becomes the sketch's own geometry of the same kind (construction stays construction), keeping what is tied to it, and no longer follows the part; then Trim cuts it. Trim on a projected edge says so instead of doing nothing. Tangent Circle takes two or three lines, arcs or circles and shows the circle from the first click; after two, a click away places it touching those two.
- No more points drawn on a shown sketch in the plain view; the building commands' dialogs still show them.
- A dimension the sketch fixes already (a circle tangent to two parallel lines given a diameter) made the sketch stop solving ("redundant constraints"); now ProstoCAD asks and adds it as a reference dimension, or takes it off.
- Shell on a part that touched itself or came from a faulty STEP brought the whole program down (inside OpenCASCADE's offset), and again on opening the file. Its arcs written as splines are now made exact first, the walls are built face by face (no offset of the whole part), and the kernel's risky offset runs in a separate process, where a crash is only a failed try; Shell works on such a faulty part too. STEP import makes arcs written as splines exact. (ProstoCAD only: the STEP import.)
- Revolve about a projected edge follows that edge: when the part changes (a Pad made 10 → 12 mm), the revolve turns about the edge where it is now, not where it was when the revolve was made. Its dialog shows the projected line again, not "Two points" with odd numbers.
- Loft: sections in order (heights 0, 10, 20) are no longer refused as "out of order" when one of the sketches faces down (drawn on a downward face, or flipped), and sections that really go back (0, −10, 20) are refused.
- A fillet or chamfer on the rim of a pocket stays on its edges when the pocket is made a little wider or moved (6 → 6.4 mm was refused with "An edge it was on is gone"): an edge that lies between the same two faces as before is found again.
- Hollow Sweep: when the profile is made smaller than the wall allows, the part no longer disappears without a word; the wall's message says the wall is as thick as the profile now. A wall too thick for an ellipse, slot or square profile is said in plain words (no "makeOffset2D: offset result has no wires").
- Hollow Sweep on a ring profile (a profile with a hole): the hole grows by the wall too, so the wall is even on both sides. A profile made thinner than the wall no longer leaves the part empty: that change is undone and the part stays as it was, with the reason said.
- Sweep with the profile away from where the path starts gave an inside-out solid (negative volume), kept with a wrong warning: it is refused, saying how far the profile is from the path's start. A path sketch not computed yet no longer gives "Sweep: TopoDS::Wire".
- Plain messages: a too-big fillet radius, or a Coil whose turns touch, says why instead of "Solid1 produced invalid geometry; Fillet produced invalid geometry" (the Solid is no longer named as well); a hole wider than the part says "make the diameter smaller"; a pattern spacing of 0 says the spacing must be more than 0.
- Pattern with Count 1 is kept (the original alone, as a count parameter set to 1 means), instead of being refused as "the pattern changes nothing".
- Sketch Offset and Mirror take projected edges too (the user's law: equal rights) - a projected outline is offset or mirrored like a drawn one; a click exactly on a line no longer breaks the Slot tool's snapping; Revolve about a construction line works also when the sketch's lines cross (its area is the profile).
- Shell with two neighbouring openings left a bar of material in their corner when the wall was more than half the inner face wide; the corner is now cut exactly.
- Fillets, chamfers, shells and drafts lost their edges or faces when the part changed size (a Pad made higher, a sketch made wider: FreeCAD's "?Edge1") and the change was refused - the commonest edit there is. The edge or face is now found again: the one of the same kind, type and direction that sits where it sat in the part (the right-hand edge stays the right-hand one when the part gets wider) - never guessed: when none or two fit, the message says to pick it again instead of "Invalid edge link: ;#f:1;...".
- Extrude / Revolve from a sketch whose outlines touch only at a corner (two holes corner to corner) failed or made two touching solids; such a sketch also offers its areas to click.
- Emboss wrapped on a round face that leaves faulty edges is kept with a warning; on a free-form face it says it can't be built there instead of OpenCASCADE's words. A pattern of cuts that splits the part into strips says so (not "copies off the part").
- Revolve's line list numbers every line by its own number, construction lines marked (two different "Line 1" before).
- A crash of the whole program: an inward 2D offset of a circle of radius 1 mm or less (a hollow Sweep of a 2 mm tube, Sketch Offset inside a 2 mm circle) brought OpenCASCADE down; a lone circle is now offset by its radius.
- Hole: a modeled tapped hole Through All ran its thread far past the part and took 7x as long (6.7 s against 0.9 s); it now goes just past the part, measured again when the part changes.
- Plain words instead of FreeCAD's and OpenCASCADE's own for: a taper that closes the profile, an empty sketch, To Next with nothing ahead, a lost To face, an open sweep profile, a wall as thick as the profile, a coil with no height or pitch or a round face as its axis, an offset the kernel couldn't do; a Draft that failed now says why. A fillet or chamfer that leaves a faulty spot is kept with a warning.
- Extrude Through All with an inward taper was refused ("values too large"): FreeCAD's Through All runs the whole box diagonal and the taper closed the profile; now it reaches just past the part, measured again when the part changes.
- Pattern / Mirror whose copies land off the part (a boss repeated past the block's end) left separate lumps in the Solid without a word, and a later Shell or Fillet failed on them; now said at OK, the copies kept.
- Editing an Extrude made as New Solid or Intersect and choosing Join or Cut silently did nothing; now it says why and what to do (Boolean, or extrude again).
- Sweep with a Wall: the inner outline was copied once, so editing the profile changed the wall (0.5 mm became 1.5 mm); now the wall is made again right after the recompute.
- Extrude Join with one shape of the profile on the part and one beside it: the whole extrude went into a new Solid made of two lumps; now it joins the part and the loose shape is pointed out.
- Revolve with two angles adding up to more than 360° gave a thin wedge (200° + 200° came out 40°): now refused, saying so.
- Loft said "The sections are out of order" for every failure, sending the user to reorder for nothing; now only an out-of-order set says that, other sets say the loft can't be made through them.
- Coil whose turns touch or overlap, or whose profile crosses the axis, is kept with a warning instead of silently.
- Hole: a hole whose edge touches a side (a wall of no thickness) gets the same warning as a cut.
- Thread: Full length and a size chosen from the shaft were measured once. A longer shaft kept its thread over the old length; a shaft made 12 mm kept its M10 groove, without a word. Now, right after a recompute, a cut thread whose shaft changed is built again (its size chosen again; a size picked by hand that no longer fits is said).
- Hole: To a face and Concentric measured the part once. A part made thicker left a To-the-bottom hole blind, and a boss moved left its Concentric hole off-centre, both without a word. Now, right after a recompute, the depth is measured again and the centres go where the round edges are (its own undo step).
- Split (Keep all): editing the knife sketch outside the Split's dialog made a piece Solid take the part's own piece (the material twice) and lost a new piece without a word. Now each piece stays in one Solid: right after the recompute a Solid left without a piece goes and a new piece gets a Solid of its own.
- A fillet or chamfer the kernel refused could spoil the feature it was built on (OpenCASCADE changes the shared edges' tolerances in place): that feature turned "Unorientable" and every next feature failed (seen after a Boolean join with a near-flush step). The feature is now computed again after such a refusal, in the dialog and on Cancel.
- Shell on a part rounded all round (every edge filleted) did nothing without a word: the kernel handed the part back unchanged and it was taken for the shell; now the next way is tried and the part is hollowed.
- Boolean with a clearance: when the tool was changed later and could no longer be grown, the Boolean failed ("Tool shape is null") and broke the part; now other ways of growing it are tried on every recompute, and if none works the cavity is cut exact, with a warning.
- Revolve about any line of the sketch: its Line of the sketch list (was Construction / projected line) offers the sketch's normal lines too, a side of the profile included; with a sketch whose lines cross (an area of it is the profile) the lines of the sketch drawn are offered, and the axis holds on to that sketch. A normal line was taken by its geometry number, which FreeCAD reads past the construction lines: the revolve failed ("Shape index out of bound").
- Loft: equal sections picked out of order (heights 0, 20, 10) folded the loft back through itself and it was kept; now it is refused, saying which section comes back.
- Sweep: a path in several separate pieces said only "TopoDS::Wire"; now it says how many pieces and what to do. A Sweep or Loft that runs through itself (a bend tighter than the profile, a closed loft crossing itself) is kept with a warning.
- Extrude / Revolve from a sketch whose closed shapes cross or touch (two overlapping rectangles, two sharing a side, a circle touching a side from inside) gave a wrong solid without a word, or failed with "invalid geometry": such a sketch now offers its areas to click, like lines that cross.
- Hide / Show while a feature dialog or an edit is open is no longer refused ("Finish the Extrude dialog first"): it is only looking.
- Boolean: a result with nothing left (Intersect of solids that don't overlap, a Cut whose tool covers the whole part) was kept as an empty Solid without a word; now it is refused with why. Solids that only touch along a line or at a point are refused too (later features failed on such a result). A new Boolean takes faces 0.001 mm apart as one: a tool a hair short no longer leaves a paper-thin skin, and two solids a hair apart join.
- Extrude Cut: a cut that touches a side along a line (a circle tangent to a wall) leaves a wall of no thickness: it is kept, with a warning, as a later fillet or shell fails there.
- A feature dialog's OK on a big part (an STL's triangles: seconds to commit) no longer frees the 'busy' state in the middle of the commit.
- Mirror Solid (Join) of a part touching the mirror plane along a line (a disc tangent to it) and Pattern copies that touch each other only along a line (discs spaced their diameter apart) came out with the right volume but faulty to the full check, without a word, and a later Shell or Fillet could fail there. The Mirror Solid join is now one sound solid (its faces made to meet on a common edge, as Extrude does); such a pattern is said at OK, its copies kept.
- Extrude and Revolve (the new own ones): a sketch, hole or fillet on their faces stays on its face when a size changes (it lost the face, and the features after it were not computed again); a Cut through a box drawn beside the part (its own Solid) is no longer refused; Extrude To a face behind the sketch goes there; Revolve about a projected line keeps its axis when that line is deleted (by hand, Break Link, or over a tapped hole). A fillet preview on a curved side (an ellipse) outlines only the round.

0.17.0
------
Improvements
- STEP export writes the edges' curves on their surfaces and offset surfaces (rounds, shells) as B-splines: other CAD programs (Plasticity and others) read the part as it is - no open faces, no edges a few millimetres off.
- Picking three points (Section by 3 Points, Work Plane ▸ Three points): after two points, a faint plane through them and the point under the pointer shows.

Bug fixes
- Extrude, Revolve and other features on a solid made of an STL's triangles took over a minute each, every preview again: FreeCAD's Refine is left off there (the triangles are merged already) and the part is checked once, not twice - about 10 s now on a 25 000-face part.

0.16.2
------
Improvements
- A chamfer wider than a face it runs onto stops at that face's far edge instead of failing (a 2.5 mm chamfer on a 2 mm face is a 2 mm one, the face taken whole); the dialog keeps the asked distance, and on a wider face the chamfer takes it again.
- Fillet and chamfer sizes start at 0.5 mm in every dialog (Fillet, Chamfer, Hole and Thread chamfers, Boss and Snap Fit fillets); their arrows step by 0.1 mm.
Bug fixes
- A click on a feature in the tree (an Emboss of a jar's label) hung for 25-30 s: its faces lit on the part were each traced back to their feature again; finding which feature made a face is many times faster on any part.
- Appearance on many faces (185 letters) took 55 s: every picked face was matched against every coloured face again on each change; now 0.5 s.
- The log names the dialog and feature of a slow preview.

0.16.1
------
Bug fixes
- An open section follows the part: a change made while it is on (a chamfer) showed as a hole in the cut, as if the new material were a surface.
- End of Part moved above the Solid another Solid's Boolean cuts with (a lid's grip ribs) was undone: the Boolean below End of Part is left out of the check.
- A feature made outside ProstoCAD's dialog (a FreeCAD file, an AI's script) opened its dialog with default values (Distance 10 mm for a 78 mm Extrude): it shows its own values.
- End of Part dropped at the bottom of the tree, below a Boolean's tool Solid (a lid's grip ribs), landed before that Boolean; it goes to the end now.
- With End of Part moved up, feature dialogs recomputed everything below it (16 s a value on a jar); what lies below End of Part is left alone now.

0.16.0
------
Much faster on big parts (a jar with a thread, a wrapped label and a lid); Interference in a part; Edit from a
face or a Solid; Esc stops long work.

Improvements
- Offset of a sketch shape shows one dimension; the other sides follow it.
- The sketch's Constraints window can be moved by its title, like the feature dialogs; the next one opens there.
- Right-click a face or an edge: Edit Feature opens the feature that made it. Right-click a Solid in the tree: Edit
  works on it with the other Solids see-through (Esc ends).
- Project Geometry on an edge or face of another Solid (FreeCAD links only the sketch's own Solid) copies its
  edges into the sketch as plain lines; they don't follow that Solid's changes.
- Esc stops a long recompute between features (FreeCAD's own stop, now also with a dialog open, no question
  asked) and InCad's long loops (the Emboss face check); one kernel operation still runs to its end.
- Interference also in a part with several Solids (Inspect > Analyze > Interference): where a jar's lid goes into the jar, in red.

Bug fixes
- A Boolean with a solid made of an STL's triangles is refused with a way round: such a Boolean could run for
  half an hour and more with FreeCAD frozen.
- A sketch in the middle of a part opened on an empty screen (everything built on it is hidden while it is open):
  the part as it is before the sketch is shown now, and the finished part comes back when the sketch closes.
  Another Solid built on this one (a lid cut by its jar) is no longer hidden with it.
- Space hides or shows what is picked again (in the model tree and in the 3D view), with InCad's own Hide / Show.
- Sketch tools (Offset and others) no longer recompute the whole part on every click: only the open sketch, the part
  follows when the sketch is finished (on a part with a thread and wrapped letters each click took 45 s).
- Boolean Cut with a clearance grows only the tool's part near the base, and again only when that part changed:
  a jar's lid was recomputed for 8 s on every change to the jar (now 1.5 s), and a jar with a wide wrapped label
  could not be grown at all. Older files get it when opened.
- Feature dialogs (Work Plane and others) open and preview without retrying a broken feature after the End of
  Part each time (8 s a preview on a jar with a failed Emboss); it is computed once, on OK. A new sketch too.
- Painted faces: every click (a tree row, a pick) worked out every face's centre again for each painted face; now once
  per shape (a lid cut by a thread hung 20 s a click).
- A Boolean as a Solid's last step showed nothing in a recovered file (FreeCAD's Group display mode draws the tools): Booleans are always drawn as their result.

0.15.0
-----
Boss, Lip / Groove and Snap Fit for printed boxes; holes for heat-set inserts.

Improvements
- Boss (3D Model > Create, the arrow beside Emboss): a post for a screw or an insert at every point or circle of a
  sketch - outer diameter, height, a plain hole or an insert's hole, a fillet at its foot, 3, 4 or 6 ribs (they stop
  at the part's outside), turned by Rib angle, any of them left out.
- Lip / Groove: on the rim of a shelled box, a raised band along the inner or outer edge, or on the other half the
  groove it goes into (wider and deeper by the clearance). It follows the rim when the part before it changes.
- Snap Fit: a flexible strip grown onto the face of a box's wall at every line of a sketch, joined
  to the wall down below the rim (its lower edge chamfered 45°) and standing up over it with a catch at its top -
  height over the rim, how far down the wall, thickness, the catch's depth and length, a fillet at the rim.
- Hole > Insert: a hole for a heat-set threaded insert, M2 to M5 - the size the insert needs, a flat bottom, 1 mm
  deeper than the insert.
- Settings > Rectangle Diagonals: a new rectangle keeps its two diagonals as construction lines (off by default:
  only the centre point).
- Settings > Check for Updates: finds a newer release on GitHub and downloads it for your system into
  Downloads; Check for Updates at Start looks once a day by itself.
- A part opened with Edit from its assembly: Return is the first entry of every right-click menu too.

- Sketch > Tangent Circle: a circle tangent to the two or three lines, arcs or circles selected (three fix it).
Bug fixes
- Boolean Cut with a clearance on a threaded part (a lid cut from a jar with a grown thread) keeps its clearance:
  it was cut with 0 mm, and the printed lid did not fit.
- A part with a modeled thread: Extrude no longer stalls for seconds - switching Join to Cut or pressing Cancel
  no longer rebuilds the whole part, and a preview no longer measures the thread's volume.
- Thread: the profile's sketch is a few lines and arcs again, not a row of short segments - threads build in a
  second or two instead of hanging the program. Custom: the shape picked is what is cut in (Cut into) or grown on
  (Grow onto) - a Triangle a sharp V, a Trapezoid that V with its end cut off, a Semicircle a round groove or a
  round bead. Grown teeth rise out of the surface from nothing over a quarter turn and run back into it at
  their end, inside the face (as on moulded canister caps); the chamfer is offered for them too.
- Thread on a hole that runs out into a curved wall: no error, and no long wait while it checks the hole's wall.
- Report a Bug could fail on other computers with "certificate verify failed": FreeCAD's Python looked for the
  certificate list where it was built.
- Screenshot (Window) of a part edited from its assembly showed the assembly's small window as a black box.


0.14.0
-----
Thread profiles and DIN threads, grown threads, a start page with recent files, Return to Assembly.

Improvements
- Thread: the list names the DIN threads that are the same (ISO metric = DIN 13, Trapezoidal = DIN 103, G = ISO
  228) and adds Round (DIN 405, Rd) and Buttress (DIN 513, S) with their sizes.
- Thread > Custom: the profile is a Triangle (its flank angle), a Trapezoid (a triangle with its tip cut off) or a
  Semicircle (as on a jar and its lid).
- Thread: Cut into the surface, or Grow onto it - teeth added on a rod or inside a bore (a jar neck's bead).
- Thread > Save for the next part: the next thread, in this file or another, starts with these settings.
- Thread on a hole that runs out into a curved wall: it starts at the hole's round mouth; the far end may be any
  shape.
- Revolve: Join, Cut or New Solid (the profile goes into a Solid of its own, for a Boolean later).
- A start page: with no file open, the window shows the recent files with their pictures; a click opens one.
- Editing a part from its assembly: a bar on the part's view says what is edited, with Return to Assembly (the part
  is saved and the assembly shows its changes). Return is also the first button on the 3D Model tab.
- Assemblies: the grounded part says Grounded over it (the padlock is bigger and in the accent colour; it often sat
  off the part); Ground still frees it.
- Split > Make Assembly: tick it and the pieces become an assembly right after OK.
- Split works from a sketch in another (even empty) Solid: it splits the Solid the sketch's lines cut.
- A profile with a loose piece (a short line that is no part of a closed outline) says where it is, in the sketch's
  own coordinates, instead of FreeCAD's "Wire is not closed".

Bug fixes
- Extrude To a face of the part from a sketch on a work plane made a separate Solid (a Boolean was needed); it joins
  the part now.
- Split with a Gap left a thin sliver where the cut line bends.
- The right-click menu of a hidden sketch whose row was selected offered only Hide; it offers Show.


0.13.1
-----
Smooth sketching; Extrude Cut off the part cuts at once.

Improvements
- While a sketch is open, the view keeps up with the mouse: drawing a rectangle, a line or anything else no longer
  lags behind the pointer (FreeCAD put off redrawing while the mouse kept moving).
- Points are easier to catch on a Mac's Retina screen: the pick radius is doubled once (Preferences > Display > 3D
  View > Pick radius; a value you set yourself stays).
- While a rectangle is drawn, its two diagonals show dashed, for orientation. The finished rectangle gets a
  construction point in its middle: put it on the origin and the rectangle is centred.

Bug fixes
- Extrude > Cut did nothing the first time when the profile lay off the part (it went into its own empty Solid, and
  Cut cut only that); Intersect and then Cut was needed. Cut now cuts the part at once.
- A rectangle's centre point could not be put on an axis: the click took the point's constraint icon. That icon is
  hidden now, also on FreeCAD's Center Rectangle.


0.13.0
-----
InCad is now ProstoCAD for FreeCAD: a new name, the same workbench.

Improvements
- InCad has a new name: ProstoCAD for FreeCAD (the workbench shows as ProstoCAD). Nothing else changes: the same
  tools, and every file made before opens as it did.
- The new home page: https://prostocad.com. The project's GitHub address is now https://github.com/Igr11/ProstoCAD
  (the old address still leads there).
- Install as before: the module folder is still called InCad, so an existing installation is simply replaced.
- The sketch's right-click menu offers Delete for whatever is selected: lines, points and dimensions. A right-click on
  something not selected selects it first, so Delete removes exactly that.
- Parameters: - deletes a sketch dimension (d1, d2...) from its sketch; one that a formula uses stays, and the status
  line says which formula.

Bug fixes
- After Symmetric the lines could not be dragged: the tool stayed on, waiting for another pair, and took every click.
  It now ends once the pair is made.
- Messages said "an InCad part"; they now read "a ProstoCAD part".


0.12.0
-----
Mirror Solid; sketch Mirror that follows its original; InCad's own Symmetric; Parameters window; Split Gap; Report a Bug.

Improvements
- Mirror Solid (3D Model > Pattern): a mirrored copy of a whole Solid as a new Solid. Select the Solid (with several,
  click the one), Mirror Solid, then click the mirror plane - an origin or work plane, or a flat face. The copy
  follows the original - every change, every feature added later - and takes features of its own.
- Mirror Solid > Result: New Solid, Join (the mirror image joined into the same Solid: a half made whole) or Cut (the
  image cut out of it). Mirror: Whole, or only the part on One side / the Other side of the plane - a part crossing
  the plane becomes symmetric with Join.
- Break Mirror Link (right-click a Mirror Solid row or its Solid): the copy keeps its shape and stops following. On a
  feature Mirror it keeps the mirrored material as it is.
- Boolean can use a mirrored Solid as a tool on its own original (Join, Cut, Intersect): the copy then follows the
  original up to the step before that Boolean.
- Sketch > Mirror: select the shapes, Mirror, then click the mirror line - any line (also one of the shape's own), the
  X or Y axis, or a point. The copy keeps the original's size and follows it, and no dimension is copied. Right-click
  the copy > Break Mirror Link frees it.
- Sketch > Symmetric is InCad's own: two points, two lines or two circles, then the symmetry line; it never picks a
  dimension, and stays on until Esc.
- Shift-click a sketch line: its whole outline is selected at once, and shows selected.
- Parameters window (View > Windows > Parameters): every parameter with its value, result and the features that use
  it; add, remove, rename, Find, Delete Unused.
- Split > Gap (in 0.05 mm steps) and Gap from: Both, This Solid or New Solids.
- Settings (gear) > Report a Bug: describe the problem, attach the log, and it goes to InCad's issues on GitHub (this
  build opens GitHub's New Issue page).
- Right-click menus show only what applies to what is under the pointer; the sketch menu is shorter (Constraints
  (n)... opens the list).
- Spur Gears / Worm Gear handles are bigger, coloured by axis, and easier to grab.
- The manual's Known limits list what Mirror Solid and clearances can't do yet.

Bug fixes
- The Parameters button only moved the focus to the small panel: it opens the Parameters window now.
- Symmetric sometimes caught a dimension's point instead of the sketch point.
- Mirror of a chain failed ("other constraints fight it") when its points lay on the mirror line.
- Boolean > Cut with a clearance refused a tool that can't be grown (an Emboss, a thread): it is cut with Clearance 0
  mm now, and the status line says so.
- Sketch Offset lit only the line clicked, not the whole outline it takes.


0.11.4
-----
Every plane of a row can be edited and turned; work features on 3D Line points and work points; work feature fixes.

Improvements
- Double-click a work plane (in the browser or in the view), or Edit on its menu: its Work Plane dialog opens. New
  Sketch on a work plane is on its right-click menu; a right-click on a work plane in the view gives its browser row's
  menu.
- Planes: every plane of a row has its own dialog - its offset along its normal and its own Turn, rings on it. With a
  row's dialog open, a click on another plane of the row keeps what was set and moves the dialog and the rings there.
- Point fields offer a 3D Line's ends and the points it passes through, and work points. Normal to edge at point on a
  segment of a 3D Line and its end gives the plane for a loft along it. A corner of a 3D Line or a work point is kept
  as that point: the work feature follows it.
- Work Plane > Angle around edge and Normal to edge at point take an origin or work axis as the edge.
- Offset and Turn step below zero with the arrows and the mouse wheel.

Bug fixes
- Only the first plane of a row could be turned: the others had no dialog (a double-click started a sketch).
- Planes typed on the second or third plane of a row made a second row on top; it now sets the whole row's count.
- The first plane of a row switched to another method kept the others tied to it; they now stay where they are, as
  planes of their own.
- Angle around edge about an origin axis failed.
- Corners clicked again in a work feature's Edit became fixed points: the feature no longer followed the part.
- On Edit, a work feature took a pick in another Solid and landed in the wrong place; it now says so.
- Work Point > Midpoint of edge on an arc or a curve was off the edge; it is halfway along the edge now.
- Work Point > Edge meets plane and Two edges meet put a point even where nothing meets; they now say so.
- Work Axis > On edge took a circle and placed a meaningless axis; it asks for a straight edge.
- A 3D Line (and a sketch's Text) could not be hidden ("Nothing to hide or show"): Hide / Show, Show All /
  Hide All Sketches and the browser treat them as sketches; a 3D Line a Sweep uses hides, as a used sketch does.
- Midplane between a face and itself was accepted.
- Picks that cannot work (parallel planes, three points in a line, the same point twice) are refused in plain words.


0.11.3
-----
Hide Edges works after the Shaded button.

Bug fixes
- Appearance > Hide Edges did nothing once the Shaded button had been used: Shaded drew the edge lines of every Solid
  whatever its setting. Shaded now shows each Solid as it is set, so Hide Edges hides its edges.


0.11.2
-----
Hole and Thread in several places at once, Apply + keeps the settings, Delete asks about what breaks.

Improvements
- Hole > Concentric: click several round edges or round faces at once (Round) - a hole at the centre of each; the
  Face is optional (the flat face beside them, the one facing you).
- Thread on several faces at once (holes or shafts): a thread on each with the same settings; afterwards each is a
  thread of its own.
- Apply + opens the next dialog with the same settings (only the picks start empty), in every tool.

Bug fixes
- Delete of a feature that others are built on (a Chamfer on a Fillet's edges) hung, then did nothing: it now asks to
  delete those too, as one undo step; No leaves the part as it was.
- Thread in a second hole: the click on it (shown as the first thread's preview) was dropped.


0.11.1
-----
Work Axis fixes: the axis of a cylinder or a cone, marked points for every Point field, the view turns while points are picked; Hide / Show no longer rebuilds the part.

Bug fixes
- Work Axis > Axis of a cylinder on part of a cylinder (a half ring) or on a cone came out across the part: it took
  the face's axis of inertia. It is now the surface's own axis, on a round edge of the face, so it follows the part;
  a face that is not round is refused.
- Every Point field of Work Plane, Work Axis and Work Point (Two points, Parallel to edge through point, Normal to
  plane through point, ...) picked a vertex blind: they now light the part's marked points (corners, edge middles,
  circle centres) as soon as they are active, also right after the Method changes. A corner keeps the feature on it;
  another marked point fixes it where it is now.
- While marked points are shown (Two points, Three points, Section by points) the view turns again with the left
  button; only pan worked.
- Show All Origin (and every Hide / Show) touched the planes and everything built on them: the whole part was
  rebuilt, 10 s on a part with embossed text, and Work Axis lagged after it. A Hide / Show choice now touches nothing,
  and work features recompute only themselves while their dialog is open.


0.11.0
-----
Spur Gears and Worm Gear: a pair of gears in mesh, or a worm and its wheel, in one dialog; they turn together in an assembly.

Improvements
- Spur Gears (3D Model > Create, split button with Worm Gear): one dialog makes a pair of gears in mesh, no sketch -
  Both gears (module, pressure and helix angle, hand), Gear 1 (teeth, width, bore), Gear 2 sized by teeth, ratio or
  centre distance; or One gear. Involute teeth (addendum 1 module, dedendum 1.25). The line under the fields says what
  the numbers make: teeth, pitch diameters, ratio, centre distance. Every number is a parameter.
- Worm Gear: the worm (axial module, 1-6 starts, pitch diameter, length, hand) and its wheel the same way; the worm's
  ends are round (the thread runs out one module before each end).
- Place: an Axis (work axis, sketch line, straight edge), a Center (a circle, a corner or a point) or a Plane; nothing
  picked: a Solid of its own at the origin, beside the gears already there. Mesh with puts gear 1 (or the worm) in mesh
  with a gear already there - a third gear for a pair - and Around it / Around gear 1 turn a gear round its mate.
- Gear 1 carries the assembly's gizmo while the dialog is open and whenever a gear of the set is clicked: arrows slide
  the pair (whole mm), arcs turn or tilt it (5 degrees); gear 2 always stays in mesh. Double-click a gear to change the
  set; deleting the first gear (or the worm) takes the second with it.
- Make Assembly puts each gear into a part file of its own and stands it on its own axis (a Rotational joint to a
  hidden, grounded Gear Axes): drag the gizmo's arc on a gear and the gears in mesh turn with it by their ratio, a worm
  and its wheel too. A part of one piece now makes an assembly of one component (a single gear).
- A long dialog scrolls its fields and keeps OK in sight.

Bug fixes
- Section: gears and worms show their cut whole (the cut through a gear's middle was hollow, a worm's in bits), and
  every shown Solid of the part gets its cut faces, not only the main one.


0.10.0
-----
Hide / Show / Show All, also in the assembly's tree; files made outside InCad edited like InCad parts; an assembly saved into a folder with its parts; a smaller gizmo that goes out; file tabs reachable.

Improvements
- The assembly gizmo is a third smaller and no longer stays on the part: a click on a part shows it for a couple of
  seconds to grab a handle, it stays while a handle is dragged or under the pointer, and then goes out; another click
  shows it again.
- Save an assembly into a folder of its name: Save (first time) or Save As writes Name/Name.FCStd at the place chosen,
  with every part of the assembly (a sub-assembly's too) saved into that folder; the assembly links to the copies, the
  files the parts came from stay as they were. Saving again keeps it all there.
- Hide, Show and Show All said outright (View ▸ Visual Style ▸ Hide / Show and every right-click menu): Hide and Show
  act on the selected solid, assembly part, plane or sketch (a hidden one by its browser row); Show All brings back
  every hidden solid of the part, every hidden part of the assembly, with nothing to pick.
- Files made outside InCad — a script's or FreeCAD's part, a STEP opened as it is — become InCad parts by themselves
  when they come to the front, with every tool: the largest Solid is the main one, a STEP's shapes become Solids where
  they are shown. No Convert button to find.

Bug fixes
- Selecting a part of an assembly lit its whole history in the browser and opened it: only the part's own row lights up
  now.
- A right-click on a part of an assembly picked the object inside the part's own file: that file became the active one
  and opened in a tab of its own, and Hide hid the part there — it vanished from the assembly with no row to bring it
  back. The right-click now picks the part as the assembly's component: Hide and Show act in the assembly's tree, and
  Show on a part's row also brings back a part hidden inside its own file.
- A part whose file was made outside InCad (by a script, in FreeCAD), opened from an assembly with a double-click, Edit
  or Open, opened as "Not an InCad part": no tools in its tab, and a Solid hidden there could not be brought back. It
  now opens as an InCad part (one Solid): the part ribbon, its history in the browser, and Undo or Hide / Show bring
  a hidden Solid back.
- With many files open (an assembly's parts opened one by one) the tabs past the window's edge could not be reached: the
  tab bar now has scroll arrows, long names are cut with …, and the full name shows when the pointer rests on a tab.


0.9.0
-----
Section, Interference, Hide / Show and Open in assemblies.

Improvements
- Section in assemblies (View ▸ Visual Style ▸ Section): the cut goes through every shown part the plane meets,
  each cut face in its part's colour with its own hatching angle; Offset, Flip and Section by 3 Points work as in a
  part. It was refused in an assembly. It also cuts STEPs, shapes from other programs and assemblies made in FreeCAD (their Bodies and shapes);
  Interference checks those too.
- Interference (Assembly ▸ Analyze ▸ Interference): where parts go into each other, every overlap in bright red over
  the parts and a panel with each pair and its volume; parts that only touch are no interference; redrawn as parts move.
- Assemblies get Hide / Show too: Show / Hide All Axes (the parts' light centre lines, remembered; a constraint
  dialog still shows them for a pick), Show / Hide All Origin and Show / Hide All Sketches.
- Right-click a part in an assembly ▸ Open: its file in its own window as a part of its own (Inventor's Open);
  Edit still opens it with the assembly around it.


0.8.0
-----
3D Line on a virtual cube, several work planes at once and turned with rings, Extrude Extents 2, Fillet Full, file pictures in Open, a Image tab, Screenshot, axes in assemblies; Sweep Wall and detached-Sweep fixes.

Improvements
- 3D Line (3D Model ▸ Sketch ▸ 3D Line): a line in space drawn on a virtual cube of points round the origin — its size
  and the step between the points are yours, written grey along its edges; nearer lines are thicker, far ones dotted,
  so the cube reads in space. Click a cube point, or anywhere on its lines (the point slides freely, grey numbers give
  the distances to the cube points either side); drag a point to move it. Lines, a Spline, or a spline Through the
  points, with a Curvature comb you can switch off. Sweep takes it as its path.
- Work Plane ▸ Offset ▸ Planes: several planes at once, 2×, 3×… the offset from the same base (for a loft); a new
  offset spaces them all, and each can still be moved on its own.
- Work Plane ▸ Turn (one compact row): X, Y, Z about the previous plane's axes or the global ones, typed or dragged on
  red, green and blue rings on the plane. The plane turns about its own point; the next one stays as it was.
- Extrude ▸ ⇄ 2: the second side has its own Extents 2 — Distance, To Next, Through All or To.
- Extrude ▸ To also reaches an edge or a work axis (through its middle), and follows it.
- Fillet ▸ Full beside the radius arrows: a full round between the two picked edges; off again, an ordinary fillet.
  Full Round Fillet has its own icon.
- File ▸ Open (and Import, Place in an assembly) shows a picture of the file under the pointer — a FreeCAD file's
  saved view, an STL, STEP or IGES drawn shaded — with its date and size, and Desktop, Documents, Downloads and the
  recent files' folders at the side.
- File ▸ Open lists only what opens: FreeCAD files, STEP and STL.
- Image tab: Insert Image (a JPG, PNG or BMP on the XY plane, 100 mm across), Scale / Transparency (click two
  points of the picture and type the real length between them — the whole picture scales, the first point staying put;
  a slider sets how see-through it is), On XY / XZ / YZ, Turn 90°, Mirror, Show / Hide. A double-click on the
  picture's row opens Scale / Transparency.
- View ▸ Screenshot (also in the File menu): the 3D view saved as PNG, JPEG or BMP at the screen's full resolution; a
  PNG can have a transparent background, for a web page.
- Assemblies show the axis of every turned body and hole (a cylinder or cone half way round or more) as a light dash-dot
  centre line; click one while Mate, Flush, Insert, Rotational, Slider, Cylindrical, Parallel, Perpendicular or Angle waits for a pick to
  use that axis.
- Image ▸ Scale / Transparency: Line ▸ Horizontal or Vertical turns the image about the first point so the line
  between the two points lies so; a magnifying glass beside the pointer while putting a point; the points are small
  and bright.
- 3D Line: a working layer — XY, XZ or YZ at the height you set (Tab / Shift+Tab or its arrows move it one step of the cube) — is bright
  and alone takes clicks, the rest of the cube a faint cage; switching layers goes through the last point. The 3D Line
  button is on the Sketch tab too (an open sketch is finished first).
- View ▸ Screenshot ▸ Screenshot (Window): the whole window — ribbon, browser, 3D view and status bar — as a picture.
  Make Assembly names each part file after its Solid and the assembly after the part + _assy; a new assembly saved on
  its first Place is named after that part + _assy.
- Assemblies: a part dragged by the mouse keeps its gizmo about 3 s (longer while the pointer is on a handle), so a
  handle can still be grabbed; the handle being dragged turns amber; the gizmo's arrow heads are smaller. Image ▸
  Scale / Transparency: the transparency slider no longer makes the image jerk; the magnifying glass shows the points
  as small crosses, not magnified.
- Tips are blue, errors red — in the dialogs and the status bar.
- Tools ▸ Material ▸ Appearance (also in a Solid's, a face's or the part's right-click menu): the picked faces or
  Solids — every Solid with nothing picked — in any colour, with a finish (Matte, Satin, Glossy, Metal, Chrome, Glass,
  Rubber), a texture over the colour (Brushed, Wood, Carbon, Knurl, Sand) and Hide Edges; shown as chosen, one Undo
  step. A coloured face keeps its colour when a feature moves it; assemblies show the parts' colours.

Bug fixes
- A Sweep's Wall came out uneven — thick on one side, thin on the other — when the profile's sketch was flipped on
  its plane (Reversed): the wall's inner outline was a mirror image of the outer one. Edit the Sweep and press OK to
  rebuild a wall made with the earlier version.
- A Sweep made away from the part, then picked in a dialog (Move Face…), was split off into its own Solid without its
  path sketch: FreeCAD repeated "links go out of the allowed scope", the dialog kept splitting it again and again and
  InnCad could crash. It now moves once, with its path (a Loft with its sections).


0.7.0
-----
Extrude To anything, Emboss round the corners, End of Part above sketches, Full Round Fillet, Show / Hide All Sketches.

Improvements
- Extrude ▸ To reaches any face of any Solid (flat or curved — a cylinder, a sphere), a work or origin plane, or any
  point (a corner, a sketch point, a work point: up to the plane through it parallel to the sketch). It follows the
  target when that moves.
- Emboss letters past the picked face run on round onto the faces that go on smoothly from it — the flat side and
  the rounded ends of a slot-shaped part, all the way round if need be — laid on them without stretching.
- End of Part can go above sketches, Texts and work planes too (it jumped back below them): they are greyed and
  hidden while below it, and come back when it goes down past them.
- Full Round Fillet (Fillet ▸ Full Round Fillet): pick the two parallel edges of a face — the end of a bar, a
  plate's side — and the face becomes a half cylinder that runs on into both sides.
- View ▸ Hide / Show ▸ Show All Sketches / Hide All Sketches: every sketch and Text of the part at once.
- Sketching on a plane inside the part makes the part see-through while the sketch is open, so the sketch shows.


0.6.0
-----
Compact ribbon, Work Plane on marked points, Section from a picked plane, slot Offset and Symmetric fixed.

Improvements
- Compact ribbon (View ▸ Ribbon Size ▸ Compact, also in ⚙): icons without names (the names are in the
  tooltips) and lower rows of small icons — the ribbon takes about 40% less height than Large.
- Work Plane ▸ Three points shows the same marked points as Section — corners, edge middles, circle centres on
  every shown Solid and the points of shown sketches — and takes three clicks on them. A corner of the part keeps
  the plane tied to it; an edge middle or circle centre places it there.
- Section builds the section from the selected flat face or plane, the XY / XZ / YZ planes from the browser
  too, with either face of the Section split button; a face or plane selected while sectioned moves the cut there.
- A constraint that repeats one the sketch has (Symmetric on a slot that is already Horizontal, Parallel on two
  Horizontal lines…) takes the older one off instead of breaking the sketch; the status line says which.

Bug fixes
- Offset of a slot (or any outline with smooth joins, like a rounded rectangle) gave "Sketch with redundant
  constraints" and the sketch stopped solving. The copy is now tied without repeats, by one offset dimension
  between two lines.
- Symmetric of a slot about an axis made the sketch fail (its Horizontal repeated the new constraint).
- Section on the XY, XZ or YZ plane cut nothing (the plane went far away). Section by 3 Points ignored a selected
  face or plane and showed its markers instead.
- The value box offered Centers / Overall / Gap for two concentric arcs or circles and failed when one was chosen.


0.5.5
-----
Construction switches only the selected lines.

Bug fixes
- Construction on a selected sketch line switched every line joined to it (the whole rectangle or
  polygon). Now only the selected lines switch; select several to switch them together.


0.5.4
-----
Emboss on a sphere, a Display Quality setting, and Revolve cut / Emboss fixes.

New features
- Emboss and Engrave on a sphere: the profile (a Text or any closed sketch, such as a star) is
  projected onto the sphere along the sketch's normal, on the side the sketch faces, and raised or
  cut along the radius. "Evenly round" is greyed out on a sphere. A profile that reaches past the
  sphere's outline, or past the edge of a cut-off sphere, is refused with a message.
- Settings (the gear at the top right) > Display Quality: Normal (faster) or Fine (smoother
  curves). Fine draws round faces with finer triangles, so a highlight on a ball or a fillet no
  longer shows facets. Default: Fine on a Mac, Normal on Windows. It changes only how the part is
  drawn: an open file is not marked as changed.

Bug fixes
- Emboss with a sketch that sits in another Solid (for example a star whose own Extrude was
  deleted) was made in that Solid, with nothing under it, so nothing appeared. It now goes on the
  Solid of the face you click, and the sketch moves there with it.
- A Revolve (or another feature) cancelled on a sketch area left a hidden copy of the area
  behind. That copy kept the sketch's projected edges construction, so a closed profile made from
  them could not be revolved or cut. The copy is now removed on Cancel (and on opening a file).
- Projected edges stayed construction when projecting took more than 6 seconds (several edges
  picked one by one); they now become normal geometry however long it takes.
- Construction on a projected edge now says what the edge is afterwards ("now normal: part of the
  profile" or "construction"): a projected edge looks the same either way.


0.5.3
-----
More speed, and a cleaner fillet preview.

New features
- Settings (the gear at the top right) > Show Log File: shows InCad.log, selected, in the Finder
  (and in the Explorer on Windows, where it sits in a hidden folder). Send it with a problem report.

Improvements
- A new or changed value (in any dialog, the value box, the Parameters panel) recomputes only the
  features that use it; it used to recompute the whole part. A Text on a part of 35 features took
  over a minute to place on a Mac; now it is instant, and so is Finish Sketch after it.
- Deleting a sketch or a feature no longer rebuilds the part from a Boolean onwards when nothing
  needs it (an unused sketch took 16 s on a part with a Boolean; now an instant). The same goes
  for everything that shows or hides features.
- Text and sketch patterns in an open sketch recompute only the sketch while you type; the part
  follows on Finish Sketch (each value took up to half a minute on a slow PC).
- The first change after opening a file with a Text no longer recomputes the Text and everything
  after it (FreeCAD marked every Text as changed on opening).
- Feature previews leave out the full geometry check (about a third of each preview); it runs once,
  on OK, and keeps the dialog open if something is wrong.
- Fillet, Chamfer and Move Face draw only the edges they make over the part, and only where the
  part does not hide them (an ellipse's seam and the far side of a ring showed through it).

Bug fixes
- A fillet preview outline that FreeCAD could not draw left an error in the log.


0.5.2
-----
Speed, and a slot's overall length.

New features
- Sketch > Dimension > Overall Dimension: click one edge of a slot (or two arcs or circles) and
  type its overall length, outer edge to outer edge. A new value makes the slot longer, not wider.
- The value box of a distance between two arcs or circles has three buttons: Centers, Overall and
  Gap (inner edges - what FreeCAD's Dimension gives on two arcs). A click switches the dimension;
  it keeps its name.

Improvements
- Big parts are much faster:
  - a click on a face of the part took up to a minute on a part with hundreds of faces; now it
    is instant, and so is the browser row lighting up the faces of its feature;
  - a whole recompute takes half the time on a part with a sketch's areas used in two solids;
  - editing an early feature: as in Inventor, the part is shown as of that feature while its
    dialog is open, and only that feature is recomputed as you type; the rest is recomputed once,
    on OK (each value typed used to recompute the whole part, and the dialog opened slowly);
  - a dimension changed in an open sketch recomputes only the sketch; the part follows on Finish
    Sketch;
  - a suppressed tapped hole no longer computes its modeled thread (3.6 s on every recompute);
  - Hole > Chamfer on a modeled thread is twice as fast.
- InCad.log starts every session with a line describing the computer, and names any InCad step
  slower than 0.1 s - send it with a report about slowness.


0.5.1
-----
New features
- File > Export... (Cmd-E): the part as STEP (.step / .stp) or STL (.stl, Normal / Fine).


0.5.0
-----
Text and Emboss.

New features
- Sketch > Text: words in a sketch that Extrude raises (Join) or engraves (Cut). Press Text (the
  cursor shows an orange Aa) and click two corners: a construction box is drawn and the text sits in
  it - Horizontal Left / Centre / Right, Vertical Top / Middle / Bottom, Fit to the box (the letters
  fill its width). Dimension or constrain the box and the text follows; a tilted box tilts the text.
  Or select a line or a circle first: the text runs along it (Start / Centre / End, Shift, Distance,
  Flip side). Font (the Mac's fonts), Bold, Italic, Size (the height of the capital letters), letter
  spacing, several lines. Mirror reads the text from the plane's other side. The text stays one
  object: double-click its row to change the words; it follows its box or curve at once while the
  sketch is open.
- 3D Model > Create > Emboss (Inventor's Emboss / Engrave): a Text or a sketch raised from or cut into
  a face. On a cylinder or a cone it is wrapped round the face (the letters keep their size, the
  height goes along the radius); on a flat face it goes straight. Around: As drawn, or Evenly round
  (the letters spread once round the whole face). Engrave may cut right through a thin wall (a
  stencil). It finds its face again when an earlier step changes.

Improvements
- Work planes, sketches and Texts made after the part's last feature show above End of Part (as in
  Inventor), not greyed out below it.
- The open sketch's Text is drawn as outlines on top (letters on a face no longer flicker into it).

Bug fixes
- A dialog that starts from its profile and still waits for a pick opens on that pick.


0.4.0
-----
Sketching, Move Face on round walls, and many fixes from testing.

New features
- Sketch > Offset is InCad's own now: one click on a line takes its whole shape (a rectangle, a
  polygon, a chain drawn line by line), the copy follows the pointer, a click places it. Corners stay
  sharp, a single line gives one parallel line (no more slot), a circle or ellipse gives a ring.
  One dimension drives the offset (Cmd-click adds more shapes, all at that distance).
- Sketch > Concentric (Constrain, after Coincident): click two circles, arcs or ellipses and their
  centres are tied.
- Move Face on round walls: a cylinder or an extruded ellipse / spline wall moves outward or inward
  by a distance (Step, Inventor or Together). One click takes the whole wall.
- Fillet / Chamfer: a click on a face takes all its edges (again: they come off); a click on an
  edge takes its smooth chain (a slot's lines and arcs, a ring in pieces).
- Circular Pattern: the axis can be any origin or work axis, a sketch line, a straight or circular
  edge, a round face, or two points clicked on the part. An axis through two points is drawn as an
  orange dashed line while the dialog is open (Revolve too).

Improvements
- While you pick, the dialog draws its result over the part as orange outlines: Fillet, Chamfer,
  Shell, Move Face and the others that show the part for picking.
- Sketch look: construction lines and shapes are orange, thinner and dashed with wider gaps;
  normal lines are a little bolder; in the dark theme the part is drawn darker while a sketch is
  open, so the sketch stands out. FreeCAD's green B-spline combs are hidden.
- Sketch ribbon: Spline is right after Line.
- Pattern along a path / Mirror in a sketch: a click on one side takes the whole shape.
- Extrude: several closed regions of a sketch are extruded together.
- Boolean: click order like Inventor - first the base (the solid that stays), then the tools.
- Threads Off / On: if some threads are on and some off, the first click turns all off, the next
  all on.
- Show All / Hide All Origin: every Solid's origin; when the origin is off screen the view zooms out
  to show it.
- Hole > Chamfer: the chamfered hole is shown (the plain hole was drawn on top of it).
- Move Face: a click near a corner picks the corner; Together follows curved walls; a chamfer or
  fillet picked with its face moves Together.
- Dimensions: a dead zone before FreeCAD's Dimension tool switches horizontal / vertical / aligned.
- No part open: the ribbon's first button is Start 2D Sketch (it makes the part).

Bug fixes
- FreeCAD hung after a Fillet on a big part (the edge picks re-selected themselves forever).
- Fillet / Chamfer: edges under a sketch's lines could not be picked; a sketch a feature uses is
  hidden; a pick on a sketch line takes the part's edge under it.
- A dialog whose window vanished (a Thread with a chamfer) blocked every command ("Finish the
  Thread dialog first"); now the next command cancels it. A dialog never stays open with dead
  buttons.
- Threads Off / On, section, measure and others failed on a part with a modelled thread
  ("undefined curve type").
- Construction / normal did not work on lines; a projected line switched to construction kept its
  colour.
- Stale "Area" faces of a cancelled region pick covered the part's edges.
- Closing a sketch while the Dimension tool ran crashed FreeCAD.
- Move Face: Together on a wall already moved Together, and flat faces that came back as B-splines.
- Hole > Chamfer on a modelled thread could come out invalid.


0.3.1
-----
Improvements
- Move Face: To also takes an edge that runs parallel to the faces (a level line, an arc, a circle)
  or a point (a corner, a work point); the faces move to its height and follow it if it moves. The
  edge or point may be on another Solid.


0.3.0
-----
Direct editing: Move Face.

New features
- New Move Face (3D Model > Modify, or right-click a face / the part): push or pull flat faces of the
  part without going back to the sketch. Pick one or more faces (they must face the same way), then
  a Distance (positive grows the part, negative cuts into it) or To a face or plane parallel to them;
  the faces move into that plane and follow it if it moves. Neighbours says what the faces next to
  the moved face do: Inventor (they keep their angle, a chamfer grows and the face gets narrower;
  holes stay holes), Step (only the face moves, a straight wall appears at a slanted neighbour's
  edge) or Together (the face and the chamfers / fillets next to it move as one piece).
- Move Face: an arrow stands on the face while the dialog is open. Drag it and the face moves with
  the preview; the Distance field follows and a label at the arrow shows the value. The arrow lights
  up under the pointer. Dragging replaces a formula or parameter in Distance with the dragged value
  in mm. With To it only shows where the face goes. Finish move on top of the right-click menu = OK.
  Distance starts at 0 mm (nothing moves until you type or drag).
- Move Face is a step in the history ("Move Face" in the browser): double-click to edit, Suppress or
  Delete like any feature; one OK is one undo step. It finds its faces again by their geometry, so
  it keeps working when an earlier feature is edited. When it cannot do the move it says why (a
  neighbour round across the move in Inventor mode, a move so large that a neighbouring face would
  vanish, a face that is no longer there, a face of another Solid) and changes nothing. Limits: flat
  faces only; in Inventor mode a neighbour that is round across the move cannot follow yet (use
  Step or Together).

Improvements
- Assembly: the gizmo arrows are a little smaller (the grab zone is as wide as before).


0.2.0
-----
Assemblies are ready to test in this build (they were untested in 0.1.x).

New features
- Assembly: drag a free part with the mouse. It moves only the way its constraints still let it
  (its own degrees of freedom); the other parts stay where they are, and a fully held part does not
  move. One drag is one undo step ("Move part").
- Assembly: click a free part to get its gizmo: an arrow for each direction it can slide, an arc for
  each axis it can turn about. Grab an arrow to slide the part, an arc to turn it. Handles are easy
  to catch (a wide grab zone on screen), the one under the pointer lights up, and the first arrow is
  up and down where the part can move that way. A click on empty space hides the gizmo.
- Assembly: each part's row in the browser shows "Grounded", "DOF n" (how many ways it can still
  move, counted against what holds it) or "DOF ?". View > Degrees of Freedom draws Inventor's DOF
  symbols on every free part; with it off, the part under the pointer shows its symbol as a tip.
- Assembly: new Parallel and Perpendicular constraints (faces or straight edges); Angle takes
  straight edges too.
- Assembly: Flip in the constraint dialogs: Mate and Flush (which way the faces face), Tangent
  (which side: outside or inside), Insert (direction), and the Rotational, Slider and Cylindrical
  joints. The preview turns the part over at once.
- Assembly: Tangent puts a round face outside the flat face's part by default.
- Assembly: the constraints in the browser (Relationships) have their own menu: Edit, Delete,
  Suppress / Unsuppress, Rename. Double-click a row to edit it. A suppressed constraint is struck
  through and its parts stay where they are. Constraint values are named after them (Mate1,
  Flush1 ...).
- Assembly: Edit on a part opens it in its own tab with the other parts of the assembly around it,
  grey and semi-transparent, at their real places (for reference only: they cannot be picked and
  are not saved). View > Assembly Context turns them off and on.
- Assembly: back in the assembly tab after editing a part, InCad asks before updating it; if you
  say no, the browser shows "Needs update" until you choose Update.
- Assembly: the browser shows each part's own history; double-click a part to open it. The part
  menu has Edit, Hide / Show, Suppress and Remove. Threads Off / On works on all parts at once.
- New Make Assembly (3D Model > Assemble, or right-click in the part): every separate piece of the
  part becomes a part file with its history, and a new assembly links them where they were (the
  largest grounded). Names are asked first; files go next to the part; the part itself stays as it
  was. Running it again offers "Replace existing files", so you don't get Train_2, Train_3 ...
- New Split (3D Model > Modify): the lines of a sketch become thin surfaces that cut the part. Keep
  all: every piece stays, each other piece as a Solid of its own (hide it, work on it, make it a
  part), still following the sketch; Keep picked: only the pieces you click stay.
- File > New Assembly in the menu. New remembers Part or Assembly; Tools > Ask on New brings the
  question back.
- Hide / Show works on Solids and assembly parts (also from their right-click menu in the browser);
  a hidden one is dimmed in the browser.
- Sketch: new Constraint List (ribbon Sketch > Constrain > List, or right-click in a sketch >
  Constraint List). It lists the sketch's constraints, including the ones with no icon to click
  (coincident points, point on a line). Pick a line or point to see only its own; select a row to
  see it in the sketch; check rows and press Delete selected (one undo step). Constraints that hold
  a sketch pattern, and dimensions used in a formula, are kept, and the window says why.
- Sketch: right-click a line or point to delete one of its constraints, or all of them.
- Sketch: projected edges are normal lines by default (as in Inventor), so they can be part of a
  profile right away. Construction switches them to construction and back. Old files follow the
  new rule in sketches nothing is built on yet.
- Hole: new Chamfer option for every hole (None / Start / Both ends, with a size): a 45° lead-in at
  the mouth of each hole and, for a through hole, at its exit. A tapped hole is chamfered from the
  thread's diameter, so a screw starts easily. With a seat (counterbore, countersink, spotface)
  only the exit can be chamfered.
- Boolean: new "Keep tool" option. Off (as it opens): the tool is used up and shows under the
  Boolean in the model tree. On: the tool stays a separate visible solid (print the pin and the box).
- Boolean: click anywhere on a solid to pick it as the base or a tool (the field names the solid,
  not the face clicked); a click on the base while picking tools is ignored. In an assembly the
  Combine button is now called Boolean too.
- Extrude: To Next goes toward the part when the default direction finds nothing; To accepts curved
  faces.
- Clearance fields say how they are measured: Boolean "Clearance (per side)", Thread and Hole
  "Print clearance (on diameter)".
- Dialogs: long choice lists wrap four buttons per row; choosing an option that needs a pick starts
  that pick, and a click on the field the dialog already made active keeps picking.

Bug fixes
- A new Solid sketched on another Solid's face took that whole Solid along with it (and Make
  Assembly then said the pieces could not be separated). It now holds only its own piece, and the
  Solid below stays shown. Older files are repaired when they are opened.
- Assembly: Mate and the other constraints picked in the 3D view sometimes lost which part a face
  belonged to, or said "can't be met" on parts placed far apart. Insert could move the grounded
  part.
- Assembly: Place asks for the part first (the save dialog for a new assembly looked like a part
  chooser).
- Delete on a Solid used by a Boolean broke the Boolean ("No source shape linked"); deleting the
  main Solid or a Split could make the other Solid vanish. Delete now asks and removes them
  together, and a pick on a piece deletes that Solid.
- A box drawn away from the part and split off into its own Solid no longer takes along what was
  built on the part after it, and sketches left on the part stay attached.
- Threads (Threads Off, Suppress) did nothing on a part with two threads when the second one was
  made after the first. Threads now attach to the hole itself; older files are repaired the first
  time threads are turned off.
- Threads Off / On left the modeled thread of a tapped Hole on (the button looked dead). It now turns
  those threads off too; the holes themselves stay.
- Threads Off / On (and Suppress on a thread) did nothing when something was made on a face of a
  later feature while the threads were off. InCad now finds the same face again by its geometry.
- Thread: choosing the Print-friendly standard sets the print clearance to 0.3 mm (0.2 mm for the
  others); a clearance you typed yourself is kept.
- Thread on a rod came out sloppy: a hair-thin fin (about 0.04 mm) stayed on every crest, worse
  when the rod was a little larger than the size (M2.5 on Ø2.594), and next to a shoulder. The rod
  is now turned down to the thread's crests first (a ThreadTrim step under the Thread); the end
  chamfers start from the part's own radius.
- Editing a thread: picks landed on the thread's own fill / bore / trim step instead of the part.
- Dialogs: a choice that becomes unavailable (after a new pick) moves to the next available one.
- Wireframe was nearly invisible in the dark theme. Its lines are now light (dark in the light
  theme) and thicker; Shaded puts the normal lines back. Switching no longer marks the file modified.
- Parameters lost their units in a file opened again (90 instead of 90°, 12 instead of 12 mm) in the
  Parameters list and in the dialogs; opening a file no longer marks its features for a recompute.


0.1.1
-----
Improvements
- Thread: any sensible size works in a hole. A Ø3 hole takes M3 (the hole is filled back to the
  M3 tap size first) or M4 (the hole is bored out to the M4 tap size first), always as a full,
  printable thread with the print clearance. The fill goes only where the hole has a wall all round,
  never into a crossing bore. A size far off the hole is still refused.
- Thread: Size "Auto" now picks the bolt that matches the hole (Ø3 -> M3, Ø4 -> M4); a tap-drill
  hole still gets its thread (Ø5.2 -> M6, Ø8.5 -> M10).
- New ribbon button "Threads" (3D Model > Modify): turns every thread off for faster work and
  redraws, and back on with a second click. A thread you turned off yourself stays off.
- Suppress / Unsuppress on a thread also turns off its chamfer and its fill or bore-out, so the
  part looks exactly as it did before the thread.

Bug fixes
- Thread on a through hole (or a rod free at both ends) started at the plain end, so the chamfered
  mouth had no thread when the thread was shorter than the hole. It now starts at the chamfered or
  rounded end.
- Thread: picking the front face as the Start face of a hole with a chamfered mouth said "The start
  face must be at one end of the threaded face". It is accepted now.
- Suppress / Unsuppress on a thread could fail with "ThreadProfile cannot be suppressed".


0.1.0
-----
First test build.
